requirements.title: Seller lists item
requirements.text: The system shall allow a seller to list an item with a starting price and an end time.
acceptanceCriteria: A seller can submit an item with a starting price and an end time and it then appears as an open auction.
A listing without a starting price or without an end time is rejected with an error message.

requirements.title: Place bid
requirements.text: The system shall allow a bidder to place a bid on an open auction item.
acceptanceCriteria: A bidder can submit a bid on an item whose end time has not passed and the bid is stored.
A bid on an item whose end time has passed is rejected.

requirements.title: Live bid updates
requirements.text: The system shall push each new bid to all clients currently watching that item without the client reloading the page.
acceptanceCriteria: When a bid is accepted, every client watching the item shows the new bid without a page reload.
A client watching a different item does not receive that bid.

requirements.title: Auction close and winner
requirements.text: The system shall close an auction when its end time is reached and declare the highest bidder the winner.
acceptanceCriteria: At the end time the item no longer accepts bids.
The bidder with the highest bid at the end time is recorded as the winner and this is shown to watchers.

requirements.title: Prices in bidder currency
requirements.text: The system shall display prices to a bidder in the bidder's chosen currency, converted using exchange rates obtained from a public exchange rate API.
acceptanceCriteria: A bidder who selects a currency sees item prices and bids converted with the latest rate obtained from the exchange rate API.
Converted prices are shown with the currency code.

requirements.title: Separate services
requirements.text: The system shall be built as separately deployable services, including at least an API server and a separate live update server.
acceptanceCriteria: The API server and the live update server run as separate processes or deployments.
Either service can be started, stopped and deployed without redeploying the other.

requirements.title: Horizontal scalability
requirements.text: The system shall allow the API server and the live update server to be scaled independently by running multiple instances.
acceptanceCriteria: With two or more live update server instances running, a client connected to any instance receives every bid for the item it watches.
Adding an instance requires no code change.

openQuestions.text: Do users need accounts and login, and what roles exist (seller, bidder, admin)? Can a seller bid on their own item?
What are the bid rules: must a bid exceed the current highest bid, is there a minimum increment, and should a late bid extend the end time?
In which currency are starting prices and bids entered and stored (seller's currency, one fixed base currency, or the bidder's)? Is the conversion for display only?
What happens if the exchange rate API is unavailable, and is there a preferred API or a limit on how old a cached rate may be?

What are the scale and latency targets (concurrent watchers, bids per second, maximum delay for a live update)? Also, what happens when an auction ends with no bids, and are payment and winner notification in scope?
